name: Morris, Joseph
what_the_sources_say: The prophet himself. The printed roll lists his followers, not Morris. His wife Mary Olsen, a Danish convert he married soon after a revelation of August 23, 1861, is probably the roll’s “Mary Morris.” The roll’s “Karen Morris” is not identified. In 1878 James Bowman, at Soda Springs, mentions a debt of “Joseph Morris’ Father in Law,” apparently living nearby; he is not named (Church History Library, MS 31876, Letters to Andrew Hendrickson, 1872–1878). His elder brother George’s reminiscences give his life before Utah, his arrival in the fall of 1853 and his earlier marriages, to Mary Thorp, Elizabeth Mills and “Elize Jones” (see Documents).
source: Anderson, Revisited, 87, 104–5; The Spirit Prevails, 149–51; George Morris reminiscences, CHL MS 1614, 115–22

name: Aggerson, Hans
what_the_sources_say: Fined $100 for resisting an officer at the March 1863 term; probably the “H. Okensen” held to bail in June 1862.
source: Deseret News, June 25, 1862, and April 1, 1863

name: Edwards, John C.
what_the_sources_say: Held to bail as “J. C. Edwards” in June 1862; fined $100 for resisting an officer in March 1863.

name: Halse, Samuel

name: Moffat, Peter
what_the_sources_say: Held to bail in June 1862; fined $100 for resisting an officer in March 1863.

name: Neilsen, Kadrup
what_the_sources_say: Convicted of murder in the second degree in March 1863 and sentenced to ten years at hard labor; pardoned by Governor Harding.
source: Deseret News, April 1, 1863

name: Parr, L.

source: Deseret News, June 25, 1862

source: Deseret News, April 1, 1863

what_the_sources_say: Held to bail as “J. E. Reese” in June 1862; fined $100 for resisting an officer in March 1863.
source: Deseret News, June 25, 1862, and April 1, 1863

name: Sorenson, John Peter
what_the_sources_say: Held to bail as “J. P. Sorensen” in June 1862; fined $100 for resisting an officer in March 1863.

name: Williamsen, S.
what_the_sources_say: Held to bail in June 1862.
source: Deseret News, June 25, 1862

name: Williams, George
what_the_sources_say: The “Prophet Cainan,” who claimed to be Morris’s successor and led the church that regathered in the Deer Lodge Valley in the 1870s; in January 1879 he wrote that the Montana Saints lived on “the Sides of the North,” where “the City of the great King” would come down before the Lord’s coming (see the Chronology).
source: Anderson, Revisited; Watson

name: Hendrikson, Andrew
what_the_sources_say: A Danish immigrant who was never a Latter-day Saint, born at Ondrup, Jutland, on July 29, 1843, and baptized into the Morrisite church in the Missouri River at Omaha on January 22, 1869 (“Record of members, circa 1869–1871,” Council Bluffs, MS 32226; translation from the Danish generated by Claude). Counselor to William James from May 1882; presided over the Montana church from 1886 until his death. His records, kept by his family, are a main source for Anderson’s book.
source: Anderson, Revisited

name: Johnson, George
what_the_sources_say: Hendrikson’s associate of more than fifty years, likewise never a Latter-day Saint; presided at the Lord’s House near Racetrack from 1921 until shortly before his death at ninety-eight, the last official leader of the Montana church. A county biography of about 1902 says he came to Montana in the summer of 1873, worked in Deer Lodge hotels, and then took up a stock ranch eight miles south of the town, and that “Johnson and his family are members of the Morrisite church.” On July 1, 1876, he married Josephine V. Oleson, a daughter of Ole Olsen of the 1861–62 roll.
source: Anderson, Revisited; Progressive Men of the State of Montana (Chicago: A. W. Bowen, [c. 1902]), pp. 1092–93

name: Beck, Lars P.
what_the_sources_say: Born in Jylland (Jutland), Denmark. Baptized at Fremont, Nebraska, on August 20, 1871, by Andrew Henriksen and Niels Jensen, with his wife Maria; their eldest daughter had been born at Fremont in 1870. Ordained a Seventy in Montana on November 10, 1872, and a member of the council of the Danish-speaking stake from 1873 to 1883; the council met in his house near Deer Lodge on February 21, 1875, and their daughter Margaret was born at Deer Lodge that May. With his brother Niels Beck he met William P. Thomas at the Deer Lodge courthouse in 1880. In February 1883 he said he could not see that choosing a president would do the church any good, and he was among the minority who would not accept William James’s election that April. Buried at Hillcrest Cemetery, Deer Lodge.
source: “Record of members, 1869–1872” (Omaha), and minutebook, 1872–1874, p. 3, MS 32226, Church History Library; council minutes, 1873–1883, MS 31876, Church History Library (translations from the Danish generated by Claude); Find a Grave 67303646

name: Beck, Maria
what_the_sources_say: Born in Slesvig (Schleswig). Baptized at Fremont, Nebraska, on August 20, 1871, by Niels Jensen and Andrew Henriksen, with her husband Lars P. Beck (above); the family settled near Deer Lodge, Montana, by 1875. Her Find a Grave memorial gives her maiden name as Christiansen. Buried at Hillcrest Cemetery, Deer Lodge.
source: “Record of members, 1869–1872” (Omaha), MS 32226, Church History Library (translation from the Danish generated by Claude); Find a Grave 67303647

name: Andrews
what_the_sources_say: Foreman and agent of the community; Davies sent him east. A former member called him the “destroying angel”; another said he left of his own accord. Given name not recorded.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Bowman, Joseph
what_the_sources_say: Called “the first born in the kingdom”; in Davies’s teaching he was counted among Davies’s sons, as Elias reincarnated. Compare Lewis H. Bowman, to whom Davies gave notes in 1879.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Cilley, Asa B.
what_the_sources_say: A blacksmith from Stockton, California, who learned the doctrine at Portland, Oregon, in the winter of 1870–71 and came to the camp in November 1871. He left in June 1879 and sued Davies with Evans and Courtney; the court awarded him $125.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Clore, Jesse Y.
what_the_sources_say: Born in Kentucky; first heard the doctrine at Gold Hill, Nevada, and took the vow at San Francisco about 1869. He lived at the camp, homesteaded four miles away, and testified for Davies in 1881 (“Jesse Y. Close” in the 1880 census).
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Corbett, Mrs. M. B.
what_the_sources_say: On Davies’s list of members in March 1881, aged 47; “Mary Corbet” in the 1880 census.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Courtney, A. J.
what_the_sources_say: At the camp from about 1876 to July 1877; a plaintiff against Davies, awarded $400.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Degroot, Mrs.
what_the_sources_say: Credited with gifts of $218, 1869–78.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81, list of donations

name: Evans, Thomas W.
what_the_sources_say: A plaintiff against Davies, awarded $2,700, the largest share. Davies said he came in 1870 and left in the spring of 1878. A Davies letter of March 1877 to a T. B. Evans, who was blind, looked for him “to come with Mr. Livingstone,” the roll’s R. J. Livingstone of Carson Valley. Emma Evans also testified.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Hagg, Ola
what_the_sources_say: Born in Sweden; at the camp from July 1868, and a witness for Davies in 1881. Probably the father of the roll’s Svend Hegg (Sven Olasson).
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Hollenbeck, Mrs.
what_the_sources_say: Credited with gifts of $195, 1869–74.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81, list of donations

name: Jones, Rachel D.
what_the_sources_say: Mrs. John E. Jones, born in Wales; a member from 1866, she came to Walla Walla with Davies in 1867. Her children were born in Utah and Montana. Her husband, sent out as a missionary in 1868 and later at Indian Valley, may be the roll’s apostle John E. Jones; that is not settled.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Kelley, Michael H.
what_the_sources_say: A sailor, born in Ireland; first came to the camp in November 1868, having learned the doctrine at San Francisco. Testified for Davies in 1881.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Lambert, V. D.
what_the_sources_say: A cooper and later a justice of the peace; Davies’s missionary at San Francisco in 1869–70. He left the community and testified against Davies. Sarah Lambert also testified.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Miller, Søren
what_the_sources_say: “Sorn Miller,” born in Denmark, at the camp from July 1868 with his wife and children Christian J., John M. and Christina, who are all on Davies’s 1881 list. Klemgard’s testimony implies that the elder Miller had been with him in Utah or at Soda Springs, that is, among the Morrisites.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Mortensen, James
what_the_sources_say: “J. Mortezen,” a shoemaker born in Sweden, at the camp from July 1868 with his wife Maria; their daughter Maria and Oscar Olsen are on the 1881 list. Whether the family connects to the Mortensens on the roll is not known.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Parker, Mrs. E. S. J.
what_the_sources_say: A widow, a member from 1868, at San Francisco. Probably the widow of Thomas Parker, Davies’s missionary there; whether he is the Thomas Parker on the roll is not settled.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Parker, Mary B.
what_the_sources_say: “Mrs. Parker of San Francisco,” credited with gifts of $2,363.40, 1868–77.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81, list of donations

name: Perkins, Cornelia S.
what_the_sources_say: Born in New Hampshire; a member from 1869 at San Francisco, at the camp from that fall. She took the minutes of meetings in shorthand, helped print the community’s tracts and taught the district school; later Davies’s second wife.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census; Find a Grave

name: Perkins, M. A. C.
what_the_sources_say: Cornelia’s mother, a member from 1869 at San Francisco, at the camp from 1872.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Roberts, Jane S.
what_the_sources_say: Born in England; at the camp from 1868, with her daughter Emily J. Roberts. Testified for Davies in 1881.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Roberts, Robert
what_the_sources_say: Husband of Jane S. Roberts; Davies’s missionary at San Francisco and Portland, who preached the doctrine and administered the vow. He was later expelled from the community and did not return.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Smith, Mrs.
what_the_sources_say: Credited with gifts of $122.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81, list of donations

name: Turnbull
what_the_sources_say: Named with Robert Roberts as administering the vow at San Francisco about 1869. Given name not recorded.
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81

name: Wood, S. W.
what_the_sources_say: A photographer, born in England, who had an upholstery shop in Portland; he heard of Davies at San Francisco in 1868, came to the camp in the fall of 1869, served as a missionary and is credited with $5,921.65 on the list of donations. A defendant in the 1880 suit (“Samuel Woods” in the 1880 census).
source: Cilley et al. v. Davies, 1880–81; 1880 U.S. census

name: Bowman, Isabella
what_the_sources_say: Killed at Kington Fort during the surrender, one of the two women shot by Robert T. Burton’s party. Burton was indicted for her killing in 1870 (the indictment was voided in 1872) and again in 1877, tried from February 18, 1879, and acquitted. Alexander Dow’s affidavit of April 1863 calls her “Mrs. Bowman, wife of James Bowman.” The 1891 Salt Lake Tribune letter says she was holding Joseph March’s baby, whom she had taken in after its mother was killed. Wife of James Bowman (below), who was still a believer at Soda Springs in 1878. Not on the printed roll; she may have joined after it was made.
source: Salt Lake Herald and Salt Lake Weekly Tribune, Feb.–Mar. 1879 (Burton trial); Salt Lake Tribune, July 26, 1891; Church History Biographical Database (Isabella Bowman); Anderson, Revisited, 148–49

name: Bowman, James
what_the_sources_say: Husband of Isabella Bowman, who was killed at the surrender. Held to bail in June 1862; fined $100 for resisting an officer in March 1863; moved to Idaho in the spring of 1863. In 1879 he testified at Burton’s trial that he had lived at Soda Springs since 1863. In August 1878 he wrote from Soda Springs to Erick Eliason in Montana, signing himself “yours truly in the New Covenant”; he had received “the Epistle so kindly sent me by the friends in Deer Lodge” and passed it on to “Father Christofferson,” and among debts owed him he lists one of “Joseph Morris’ Father in Law” (Church History Library, MS 31876, Letters to Andrew Hendrickson, 1872–1878). Not the John Bowman of the roll, who was at Kaysville in 1870 and South Weber in 1880; Anderson also treats them as two men.
source: Deseret News, June 25, 1862, and April 1, 1863; Salt Lake Herald, Feb. 21, 1879; Anderson, Revisited, 148, 162; Church History Biographical Database (Isabella Bowman)

name: Søndermark, Anders
what_the_sources_say: Born at Vrensted, Jylland, Denmark, January 9, 1821; entered in the draft register as Anders Sørensen, an Aaronic priest. Baptized at South Weber on July 31, 1861, “by Morrisen og Mikkelsen” (by Morris and Mikkelsen), and confirmed by Joseph Morris; a member of the Omaha congregation from 1869, and probably the “Bro. Søndermark” of the Fremont council of November 30, 1871, who said he believed “J. Morris was a Prophet.” Excluded from the Omaha congregation on November 30, 1871. Not on the printed roll.
source: “Record of members, 1869–1872,” and its draft, “Record of members, circa 1869–1871” (Omaha), MS 32226, Church History Library; translation from the Danish generated by Claude; Fremont council minutes, November 30, 1871, MS 31876

name: Søndermark, Karen Sørensen
what_the_sources_say: Born at Vrensted, Jylland, Denmark, October 9, 1822; entered in the draft register as Karen Maria Sørensen; wife of Anders Søndermark. Baptized at South Weber on July 31, 1861, “by Morrisen og Mikkelsen,” and confirmed by Joseph Morris; a member of the Omaha congregation from 1869; excluded on November 30, 1871. Not on the printed roll.
source: “Record of members, 1869–1872,” and its draft, “Record of members, circa 1869–1871” (Omaha), MS 32226, Church History Library; translation from the Danish generated by Claude

name: Knudsen, Hans
what_the_sources_say: Born on Fyn, Denmark. Baptized at South Weber on July 18, 1861, by Jens Mikkelsen and confirmed by Joseph Morris; a leading member of the Council Bluffs congregation from 1869, baptizing and confirming others there and at Omaha and Crescent City. Not on the printed roll.
source: “Record of members, circa 1869–1871” (Council Bluffs), MS 32226, Church History Library; translation from the Danish generated by Claude

name: Fellows, Carleton
what_the_sources_say: Born at Buffalo, New York, August 15, 1809. Baptized at Omaha in 1869 by S. P. Guhl and Hans Knudsen; husband of “Maria Fellows, formerly Maria Guhl,” who had been baptized at South Weber. In 1869 Williams told him he had been Jonas, the father of Simon Peter. Both were excluded from the Council Bluffs congregation on February 5, 1871.
source: “Record of members, circa 1869–1871” (Council Bluffs), MS 32226, Church History Library; translation from the Danish generated by Claude; record book, 1869, MS 31876
